answer: Each epoch publishes an unpredictable nonce, and every submission must carry a value derived from that nonce and the agent's key. Peers recompute it before attesting, so text written before the epoch opened cannot pass. A farm can no longer stockpile one answer for a thousand keys; each identity needs its own live generation after the nonce exists. No two opals share a pattern, and no two valid derivations should either, so reuse is cheap to detect. Cost moves from one purchase at the dawn of a campaign to a per-identity, per-epoch bill; a meadow grazed by too many herds feeds none of them.
